title: When does a neuron explanation actually work?
description: Leo Gao's research discussion explained in three passes per idea: the technical statement, an eighth-grade restatement, and the simplest faithful explanation. Original diagrams are illustrations, not experimental results.

scenes.heading: Labels can miss activation detail
scenes.narration: A semantic label alone may miss a neuron's activation selectivity and magnitude.

scenes.heading: A name may leave things out
scenes.narration: A name for the pattern may leave out which examples a neuron responds to, or how strong each response is.

scenes.heading: When, and how much?
scenes.narration: A name can miss things: when it reacts, and how much.
labels: A name is only a clue

scenes.heading: Test simulated activations
scenes.narration: The proposed test: replace actual activations with predicted values, then measure downstream Kullback Leibler divergence, or KL divergence, across many inputs.
scenes.concept_title: How do we test an explanation?

scenes.heading: Compare the likely answers
scenes.narration: Predict the neuron's response, then put that prediction into the network. Across many examples, compare the chances of different answers before and after the swap.
scenes.concept_title: How do we test an explanation?

scenes.heading: Try your explanation inside
scenes.narration: Try the predicted numbers inside the model. Across many examples, do the chances of each answer change?
scenes.concept_title: How do we test an explanation?

scenes.heading: A proxy, not a full explanation
scenes.narration: Downstream KL is an imperfect evaluation proxy, and neuron-level explanations alone do not explain inter-neuron computation. This is a methodological argument, not an empirical result.

scenes.heading: The parts are not the whole
scenes.narration: This is a proposed way to test explanations, not a new experiment. The comparison has limits, and individual neurons don't explain how the network works as a whole.

scenes.heading: A check, not the final answer
scenes.narration: It's a proposed check, not a new experiment. It has limits: understanding the parts doesn't mean we understand the whole.

scenes.heading: Read the full argument
scenes.narration: These ideas come from Leo Gao's research discussion, Neural networks are not already clean. Read the full post for its argument and caveats.

claims.text: A plausible pattern among activating examples is not sufficient to establish that a neuron is explained.
A neuron can respond to only a subset of the situations matching a proposed label.
Activation strength may carry important information that a category label leaves unexplained.
Gao proposes predicting activations and substituting the simulated values to check whether model behavior is preserved.
Gao proposes evaluating explanations with downstream KL divergence over a large dataset.
Gao considers the KL metric imperfect; individual neuron explanations are only part of understanding the network.

limitations: This source is a research argument, not a new empirical demonstration.
Downstream KL is an imperfect test; preserving it does not establish complete understanding or general AI safety.
Understanding individual neurons does not by itself explain the computations between them.
